samples.summary: Author-only edit/delete gate is enforced only on the REST path, and its authorization subject (`author.userId`) is peer-writable CRDT data
samples.evidence: `assertCommentAuthor` (comments.controller.ts:519-534) decides edit/delete authority by comparing the *stored* `comment.author.userId` against the caller. That value lives inside the Yorkie document, which is directly read-write for every workspace member and for any share-link holder with role `editor` — see `packages/backend/src/document/yorkie-auth.controller.ts:202` (membership grants rw on the whole document, "the model has no per-member viewer role today") and :217 (`needWrite ? link.role === 'editor' : true`). Two consequences: (1) any workspace member can bypass the gate entirely by editing/deleting another user's comment straight over Yorkie from the editor; (2) a peer can rewrite a victim's `author.userId` to their own over Yorkie and then use `PATCH/DELETE .../comments/:threadId/comments/:commentId` — i.e. the gate's input is attacker-controlled. The gate therefore only binds credentials that have an API key but no Yorkie/JWT access, while the controller docblock (lines 106-110) and the docs/design/sheets/comments.md hunk present it as the server-side enforcement of the lifecycle rule. Additionally the webhook that would even restrict Yorkie access is in shadow mode unless `YORKIE_AUTH_WEBHOOK_ENFORCE=true` (yorkie-auth.controller.ts:100-119), in which case *anyone* with a valid token gets allowed.

samples.summary: `tabId` route param is used as an unfiltered object key for both the existence check and the write, giving a prototype-pollution shape (`PUT .../tabs/__proto__/images`)
samples.evidence: `worksheetOrThrow` does `root.sheets?.[tabId]` (line 57) with `tabId` taken verbatim from the URL. For a plain-object root, `sheets['__proto__']` resolves to `Object.prototype`, which is truthy, so the `if (!worksheet) throw NotFoundException` guard passes; `setImages` then executes `ws.images = {}` (line 111) and `ws.images[image.id] = image` (line 112) against `Object.prototype`, polluting every object in the process (`{}.images` becomes truthy). The same key is also used to reach the write inside `doc.update`, so the check and the mutation share the bad key. In production `root.sheets` is a Yorkie object proxy whose `get` trap likely answers `undefined` for an absent key, which would neutralise this — I could not confirm the SDK's trap because node_modules is not present in the tree, hence low confidence. The identical pattern already exists in `worksheet-charts.controller.ts:49`, so this is a copied rather than novel shape, but the new route adds a second reachable entry point. `image.id` is likewise unfiltered as an object key (line 112).

samples.summary: Comment writes call `NotificationService.createFromComment` directly, bypassing the per-user anti-abuse throttle that guards the browser's reporting route
samples.evidence: `POST /notifications/comment` is deliberately capped at 30 requests/min per authenticated user by `UserThrottlerGuard` + `@Throttle({ ttl: 60_000, limit: 30 })` (notification.controller.ts:63-65), whose docblock states the limit exists because it "is the one endpoint a client can call on its own initiative" and that IP keying "leaves an attacker with several source addresses effectively uncapped". The new controller calls `this.notificationService.createFromComment(actorId, plan)` in-process (comments.controller.ts:206), so only the global IP-keyed bucket applies (`ThrottlerModule.forRoot({ ttl: 60_000, limit: 120 })`, app.module.ts:97-103). A workspace member holding a write-scoped API key can therefore post 120 comments/min, each mentioning up to `MAX_RECIPIENTS` (20) members with a fresh `commentId` that defeats the dedupe index — ~2400 notification rows/min from one IP, and unbounded across several. docs/design/notifications.md acknowledges the bypass but justifies it only as "bounded by the one-comment-per-request shape", which does not bound the rate.

samples.summary: Plans are cast to `CommentNotificationDto` and passed to the service without the class-validator constraints that only run on the HTTP route
samples.evidence: `planCommentNotifications({...}) as CommentNotificationDto[]` (comments.controller.ts:197-203) fabricates a DTO instance without any ValidationPipe. The DTO's constraints — `@MaxLength(200)` on `threadId` and `commentId`, `@ArrayMaxSize(50)` on `recipientUserIds`, `@MaxLength(2000)` on `preview` — are enforced only by the global pipe on `POST /notifications/comment`. Here `threadId` is the raw route parameter (arbitrary length, attacker-chosen) and flows into `dedupeKeyFor` → `` `${dto.threadId}:resolved` `` (notification.service.ts:91) which is written to the unique-indexed `dedupeKey` column. An oversized or unusual value reaches Postgres unvalidated; the resulting error is caught and only logged by `notify`, so the failure is silent. Recipient count is still capped by the service's own `MAX_RECIPIENTS` slice, and `preview` is still passed through `sanitizePreview`, which limits the blast radius.

samples.summary: `parseImages` accepts any non-empty string as an image `src` — no scheme or origin allowlist on a URL that every viewer's browser will fetch
samples.evidence: `src: requireString(i.src, 'src')` (worksheet-images.ts:55) is the only check; the docblock says the value is "stored verbatim". The frontend renders it via `resolveImageSrc(image.src)` / `getOrLoadImage(image.src)` into an `` (image-object-layer.tsx:195-196), so a write-scoped API key can plant `https://attacker.example/beacon.png` into a shared worksheet and harvest every viewer's IP/User-Agent, or a `data:`/`javascript:` URI. The repo already treats this field as attacker-controlled — `share-image-url.ts:18-26` calls its origin check "a SECURITY boundary" precisely because "`data.src` comes from the CRDT and a malicious collaborator can set it" — but that defence only prevents share-token leakage, not the outbound fetch itself. No scheme/origin allowlist exists on the write path. Searched: `packages/backend/src/yorkie/worksheet-images.ts` (whole file), grep for `SheetImage` across the repo, `packages/frontend/src/api/share-image-url.ts`, `packages/frontend/src/app/spreadsheet/image-cache.ts`, `packages/frontend/src/app/spreadsheet/image-object-layer.tsx`.
searchedFor: grep for allowlist/scheme validation on src

samples.summary: `copyComment` dereferences `c.author` without a guard, so one malformed comment written by any CRDT peer makes `GET /comments` 500 for the whole document
samples.evidence: `copyComment` calls `copyAuthor(c.author)` (comment-ops.ts:76) and `copyAuthor` reads `a.userId` (line 68) with no null check. `isThread` (the only entry guard) validates that `comments` is array-like but never that each element has an `author`. Any workspace member or share-link editor with direct Yorkie write access (yorkie-auth.controller.ts:202/:217) can store a comment object without `author`; every subsequent `GET .../comments`, `POST .../replies`, `PATCH` and `DELETE` on that document then throws a TypeError inside `listThreads`/`copyThread` and answers 500 — an availability denial of the whole comment surface for that document. `commentAuthorId` (line ~160) does use optional chaining, showing the missing-author case was anticipated elsewhere in the same file.

samples.summary: New controller hand-rolls a private copy of the workspace-scope + sheet-type gate instead of the shared `assertSheetDocument` util that exists because copies of it drift
samples.evidence: `ApiV1WorksheetImagesController.assertSheetDocument` (lines 40-51) reimplements `packages/backend/src/api/v1/sheet-document.util.ts#assertSheetDocument`, whose docblock states: "Nine controllers carried a private copy of this method... the copies are what let the cells one go missing until #1019, so the logic lives here once." The sibling `ApiV1WorksheetChartsController` at the same route prefix uses the shared util (worksheet-charts.controller.ts:36-43). The copy here is currently correct (it does pass `workspaceId` to `getDocumentOrThrow`), so this is a duplication of a security-relevant gate rather than a present hole — but it is the exact drift vector the util was extracted to close.

The gate therefore only binds credentials that have an API key but no Yorkie/JWT access, while the controller docblock (lines 106-110) and the docs/design/sheets/comments.md hunk present it as the server-side enforcement of the lifecycle rule. verdict.reason: Every element of the finding checks out in the repository. `assertCommentAuthor` (comments.controller.ts:519-534) is the sole authorization gate for editComment (:431), deleteThread (:460-464) and deleteComment (:502), and it decides authority by comparing the *stored* `comment.author.userId` — data that lives inside the Yorkie CRDT — against the caller. That data is directly writable by every principal the gate is supposed to bind: yorkie-auth.controller.ts:193-207 grants workspace members access with no read/write distinction (the comment there states "Membership grants read+write; the model has no per-member viewer role today"), and :217 grants rw to any share-link holder with role `editor`. The alternate write path is unmediated in practice: packages/frontend/src/app/spreadsheet/yorkie-worksheet-comments.ts:100-125 edits a comment body and splices a comment out of a thread by id with no author check whatsoever, the author-only rule existing only as a UI render condition at CommentThreadCard.tsx:92. So (a) a member or share-link editor can perform the exact operation the gate refuses by writing the CRDT directly, and (b) the gate's own input can be rewritten over Yorkie before calling PATCH/DELETE .../comments/:threadId/comments/:commentId. The controller docblock at :106-110 and :513-517 nonetheless presents this as the server-side enforcement of the author-only lifecycle rule, so it reads as covered when it is not. Additionally yorkie-auth.controller.ts:100-101 and :111-119 confirm the webhook converts every deny into an allow unless YORKIE_AUTH_WEBHOOK_ENFORCE === 'true', so even the coarse document-level check is off by default. I weighed refuting on the grounds that no trust boundary is crossed (bypassers already hold document rw, so they gain no authority they lacked), but that is an impact judgment rather than a named refutation ground: the code is present exactly as described, no guard elsewhere makes the bypass unreachable, and an authorization decision keyed on peer-writable data is squarely in the authorization/access-control lane. Under the rule that uncertainty keeps the finding, this stays.

finding.summary: `tabId` route param is used as an unfiltered object key for both the existence check and the write, giving a prototype-pollution shape (`PUT .../tabs/__proto__/images`)
finding.evidence: `worksheetOrThrow` does `root.sheets?.[tabId]` (line 57) with `tabId` taken verbatim from the URL. For a plain-object root, `sheets['__proto__']` resolves to `Object.prototype`, which is truthy, so the `if (!worksheet) throw NotFoundException` guard passes; `setImages` then executes `ws.images = {}` (line 111) and `ws.images[image.id] = image` (line 112) against `Object.prototype`, polluting every object in the process (`{}.images` becomes truthy). The same key is also used to reach the write inside `doc.update`, so the check and the mutation share the bad key. In production `root.sheets` is a Yorkie object proxy whose `get` trap likely answers `undefined` for an absent key, which would neutralise this — I could not confirm the SDK's trap because node_modules is not present in the tree, hence low confidence. The identical pattern already exists in `worksheet-charts.controller.ts:49`, so this is a copied rather than novel shape, but the new route adds a second reachable entry point. `image.id` is likewise unfiltered as an object key (line 112).

verdict.reason: The code is present exactly as described: worksheet-images.controller.ts:53-60 resolves an unfiltered `tabId` route param as an object key (`root.sheets?.[tabId]`) and gates on bare truthiness (`if (!worksheet) throw new NotFoundException`), then setImages (lines 106-113) reuses the same key to reach `ws.images = {}` and `ws.images[image.id] = image`. No caller-side or guard-side normalisation exists: the route's @UseGuards (line 33) are auth/scope only, and the membership-test helper `safeWorksheetRecordKeys` is used in exactly one file (worksheet-structure.controller.ts), not here. The repository itself documents this guard shape as exploitable: worksheet-structure.controller.ts:80-113 states the bare `if (!worksheet)` check was replaced precisely because the Yorkie proxy's get trap answers `getID`/`toJSON`/`toJS`/`toString` with a truthy function, so `.../tabs/toString/insert` walked past it and handed the engine a function to mutate, and worksheet-structure.controller.spec.ts:70-81 regression-tests `__proto__`/`constructor`/`toString` as tab ids there; worksheet-images.controller.spec.ts has no such test. The only mitigating point I could establish is the same comment's claim (worksheet-structure.controller.ts:88-90) that `__proto__` specifically returns undefined through the proxy because the trap reads a real Map, which would defuse the literal Object.prototype-pollution chain -- but @yorkie-js/sdk (pinned 0.7.19, packages/backend/package.json:49) is not vendored in the tree, so I could not verify the trap independently, and that mitigation would not cover the method-name keys the repo says do slip through. No named refutation ground applies: the code is not absent, is not guarded elsewhere, and an attacker-controlled key reaching a write path through a bypassable existence check is squarely in the authorization/unsafe-input lane. Confidence is low because the specific prototype-pollution impact is unconfirmed, not because the weakness is doubtful.

finding.summary: User-controlled `:tabId` is used directly as an object key and then written into (`ws.images = {}`), so a request with `tabId=__proto__` can reach an assignment onto `Object.prototype` if the root ever behaves like a plain object
finding.evidence: `setImages` takes `:tabId` straight from the URL (Express URL-decodes, so `%5F%5Fproto%5F%5F` → `__proto__`) and does `root.sheets?.[tabId]` in `worksheetOrThrow` (line 51-57). On a plain JS object `sheets['__proto__']` returns `Object.prototype` — truthy — so the NotFound guard passes and `doc.update` then executes `ws.images = {}` followed by `ws.images[image.id] = image` (lines 97-98), writing attacker-controlled data onto `Object.prototype`. Against a real Yorkie object proxy the outcome depends on the SDK's `get` trap (the SDK is not installed in this tree, so I could not confirm which way it falls); the controller's own spec harness uses a plain object, which is the shape where this is exploitable. Note the identical pattern already exists pre-change in `worksheet-charts.controller.ts:106-110`, so this is a new instance of an existing pattern rather than a new class. A cheap fix is to reject any `tabId` that is not present in `root.tabOrder`, or to use `Object.prototype.hasOwnProperty.call(sheets, tabId)`.

verdict.reason: The code is present exactly as described. worksheet-images.controller.ts:53-60 resolves a user-controlled `:tabId` with a raw dynamic index and only a truthiness guard (`const worksheet = root.sheets?.[tabId]; if (!worksheet) throw ...`), and setImages (lines 91-113, writes at 111-112) passes the unvalidated param straight through to `ws.images = {}` / `ws.images[image.id] = image`. The class guards at line 33 are auth/scope guards only and do not constrain tabId, so nothing upstream makes the sink unreachable. The repository itself confirms this is a real, exploitable class of bypass: worksheet-structure.controller.ts:80-113 replaced the identical bare truthiness check with a key-membership test (`safeWorksheetRecordKeys(sheets).includes(tabId)`), documenting that `.../tabs/toString/insert` "walked past a bare `if (!worksheet)`" because the Yorkie proxy get trap returns truthy functions for getID/toJSON/toJS/toString, and worksheet-structure.controller.spec.ts:70-81 asserts `__proto__`/`constructor`/`toString` must be rejected (noting `sheets['__proto__']` is `Object.prototype`, truthy, on a plain object). One caveat: that same comment (lines 88-90) says `__proto__` happens to resolve to undefined through a real Yorkie proxy, so the exact Object.prototype-pollution vector may not fire in production (the SDK is not installed in this tree, so I could not verify the trap myself); however the gate is still bypassable in production via the truthy function keys, so the finding stands as a real missing-validation/unsafe-key-handling defect rather than something I can concretely refute. No refutation ground (not-present / already-guarded / out-of-scope) applies.
